title: The study's sites: about {c[st-001][value]:.0f} TWh a year, more than Oregon, Idaho, or Montana, about nine-tenths of Washington
subtitle: A Nature Sustainability analysis of {c[st-002][value]:.0f} validated hyperscale sites, May 2024 to April 2025; not every data center and not the national total. State bars are 2025 retail sales reported to EIA, which already include each state's data centers; hollow marks are the study's modeled estimates, filled marks are reported sales, in TWh a year.
text: Oregon's hyperscale sites drew about {c[st-004][value]:.0f} TWh; Washington's about {c[st-005][value]:.1f} TWh, at roughly {c[st-008][value]:.0f} g CO2 per kWh on its grid against {c[st-007][value]:.0f} in Oregon and {c[tr-038][value]:.0f} across the study. Idaho and Montana have no hyperscale site in this sample, which does not count all data centers in either state.
boundary: Modeled estimates and reported sales, not metered load; the study covers twelve months ending April 2025, the state figures calendar year 2025.

details: Electricity is estimated as facility capacity times hours times a scenario-based load factor, assigned to a grid region, with carbon from the region's plant mix.
The study covers twelve months ending April 2025; the state figures are calendar year 2025.
The facility list comes from commercial data, and a co-author works for its provider, as the paper declares.
